newsitem.title: UK: UK proposes allowing limited liability partnerships.
newsitem.headline: UK proposes allowing limited liability partnerships.

text.p: The British government on Thursday proposed new legislation to allow the introduction of limited liability partnerships for professional businesses.

Board of Trade President Ian Lang said in a statement the government planned to make limited liability partnerships available to regulated businesses in Britain to protect both partners and the public.
Lang said limited liability partnership was widely available in the U.S. and some other countries and said Britain needed new legislation to avoid undermining business confidence.

"The proposals are being made in response to concerns that, under present partnership law, the personal assets of the active members of the partnership are at risk from the business decisions of other partners even though it may well be impossible for partners even to know all the other partners," he said.
He said the proposals aimed to safeguard partners against unlimited personal liability for matters in which they were not personally at fault.

In addition, the proposals included ways to protect people dealing with partnerships, including public disclosure of information about the partnership and safeguards in the event of insolvency, he said.

At present, partners can only limit their liability for a firm's debts if they do not become involved in business management. Partners can also limit liability by incorporation as a limited liability company, Lang said, citing accountancy partnership KPMG as an example.
KPMG said in a response it welcomed the proposals.

"KPMG believes any limiting of liability has to be combined with full disclosure of financial information. That is why we led the way with incorporation two years ago and now publish full audited accounts for the whole of KPMG," KPMG said.
